assessment.margin_of_the_call: The model put home at 0.3597 and away at 0.3559 -- 0.38 percentage points apart. Pinnacle put away at 0.3452 against home 0.3428, 0.24 apart. Both were near-coin-flips; the market's lean was the right one and the model's was not.
assessment.the_stand_down_was_right_for_the_stated_: The decision was no bet because the best selection sat below the edge threshold and was the signal H-0003 measures as pointing the wrong way. That reasoning is unchanged by the result. Backing Lazio at the 2.60 available retail would have won -- and at 7.80% below Pinnacle's near-close it sits in the CLV band measured at -16.14% over 8,035 bets. A winning bet taken at a bad price is still a bad bet.
assessment.what_this_settles: Nothing. One match. The outcome that happened had a probability of about 0.35 under every source here, including the ones that got the lean wrong.

why: Best selection is home at +2.53% EV, below the 5% edge threshold the value rule requires. More decisively, H-0003 measures the model's disagreement with the price as a measure of the model being wrong, and the 'edge >= +3% on the home side' rule returned -7.2% (t = -3.31) over 3,004 Serie A matches.
